other people are in them, so ownership has to move or the workspace has to be
deleted first. One already scheduled for deletion carries `deletion_scheduled`

Rendered from one batched user read per page rather than stored on the row, so

Exactly one of `url`, `slack_channel_id` and `discord_channel_id` is given. The
`*_channel_name` fields are only the name the picker showed, kept so the list
can say where it posts.

One Slack or Discord channel a team, or the whole workspace, posts its notifications to.

`disabled_reason` is set when the channel answered 404 or 410 and was turned

and lists the teams it follows in `team_ids`, empty for every open team.

Change a channel, leaving unset fields alone.

notice an automatic disable left.

CheckoutCreate.title: CheckoutCreate

CommentAnchor.description:
The passage of the issue description a root comment is pinned to.

The quoted text plus a little of the text either side, which is what finds the
passage again among repeats of it. Never written into the description, so an
edit that removes the passage leaves the quote here and the reader shows it as
changed.
CommentAnchor.title: CommentAnchor

CommentCreate.description:
The body a comment create takes.

`attachment_ids` names attachments already on the same issue, uploaded or
linked first through the attachment routes, which the comment then shows
inline. The route holds that each one exists under this issue. The body may
be empty only when the comment carries an attachment, so a screenshot can be
posted without a caption while a comment is never blank. `anchor` pins a new
thread to a passage of the description, so a reply cannot carry one.
CommentCreate.title: CommentCreate

CommentRead.description:
One comment as the API returns it.

`github_thread` is set on a root comment whose thread is synced to a GitHub
pull request or issue, and `resolution` on a root whose thread is resolved,
which a reader collapses to one line. `anchor` is set on a root pinned to a
passage of the issue description.
CommentRead.title: CommentRead

CommentUpdate.description: The body a comment edit takes, carrying the issue that partitions it.
CommentUpdate.title: CommentUpdate

ConnectedAppListRead.description: The caller's connected apps, most recently used first.

ConnectedAppMemberRead.title: ConnectedAppMemberRead

`new_scopes` are scopes the product offers that some grant does not cover yet,
usually because they were added after the client was authorized.

ConnectedAppWorkspaceRead.title: ConnectedAppWorkspaceRead

four buckets agree with a fifth counter that could drift from them.

straight into the `app` secret and are never answered.

`can_edit` and `can_delete` say what this caller may do, so a client draws

CustomerRequestCreate.title: CustomerRequestCreate

`customer_id` hands the request to another customer, and `target_kind` with

CustomerRequestRead.description:
One request, with the names a list draws beside it.

`target_key` is the issue key for an issue and empty for a project.
CustomerRequestRead.title: CustomerRequestRead

CycleCalendarFeedRead.description:
The caller's cycle calendar feed for one team.

`url` carries the feed token, so it is answered only by the call that minted
it: the token is stored as a hash and cannot be read back. A read of an
existing feed says it is `active` with a null `url`, and minting again revokes
the old URL.
CycleCalendarFeedRead.title: CycleCalendarFeedRead

CycleCapacityRead.description: The active or next cycle's current scope, which capacity guidance weighs.
CycleCapacityRead.title: CycleCapacityRead

CycleHistoryPoint.description:
One day of a cycle's burn-up, in issues and in estimate points.

`scope` excludes cancelled work, `started` includes finished work, and
`completed` is finished work alone, matching the cycle page's own figures.
CycleHistoryPoint.title: CycleHistoryPoint

CycleHistoryRead.description: A cycle's daily scope history, first day to today or its end.
CycleHistoryRead.title: CycleHistoryRead

CycleRead.description: One cycle as the API returns it, with its status derived from its dates.
CycleRead.title: CycleRead

CycleSettingsRead.description: A team's automatic cycle settings as the API returns them.
CycleSettingsRead.title: CycleSettingsRead

CycleSettingsUpdate.description:
The body a team's cycle settings patch takes, every field optional.

`start_weekday` counts from Monday as 0 to Sunday as 6.
CycleSettingsUpdate.title: CycleSettingsUpdate

CycleStartTodayRead.description:
What starting a cycle today changed.

`ended` is the cycle that was current, now ending yesterday, or null when no
cycle was running. `moved_issues` counts its unfinished issues rolled into
the started cycle.
CycleStartTodayRead.title: CycleStartTodayRead

The body a cycle patch takes.

`team_id` is required rather than patchable: it names the partition prefix
the row is filed under, and moving a cycle between teams would orphan every
issue pointing at it.

DeliveryAttemptRead.description:
One try at posting a delivery: what came back and how long it took.

`status_code` is 0 when no HTTP response arrived, in which case `error` says why.

DiscordChannelRead.description: One Discord text or announcement channel the bot can post to.

DiscordInstallUrlRead.title: DiscordInstallUrlRead

Whether the caller's personal notifications reach their Discord direct messages.

`available` says the workspace has the Discord App in a server, `linked` that
the caller has a route, and `problem` why that route cannot deliver right now,
such as closed DMs or the App leaving the server, which a new link clears.
Nothing here names another member or carries a token.

DiscordLinkUrlRead.description: Where to send the caller to link their Discord account, and when that link stops working.
DiscordLinkUrlRead.title: DiscordLinkUrlRead

DisplayOptionsBody.description:

Held to the saved view's own choices, so a team default is always one a view
could save: a sub grouping needs a grouping and must differ from it. Either
grouping may be `none`, which a page reads as no grouping rather than as its
built-in one.
DisplayOptionsBody.title: DisplayOptionsBody

DocumentCreate.description:
The body a document create takes; the parent comes from the path.

`template_id` names a document template the parent offers. Its title fills
a left out `title`, and its body a left out `body`; a create without either
a title or a template is refused.
DocumentCreate.title: DocumentCreate

DocumentMentionRead.description: One issue a document mentions, as its key was written.
DocumentMentionRead.title: DocumentMentionRead

DocumentPatch.description:
The body a document patch takes; any field may be left out, and only `icon` cleared.

`parent_kind` and `parent_id` together move the document under another
project, initiative or team the caller may write under. `base_updated_at`
is the `updated_at` the editor last read. When it is sent and the document
has changed since, the patch is a 409 rather than writing over someone
else's edit.
DocumentPatch.title: DocumentPatch

DocumentRead.description: One document with its Markdown and the issues it mentions that this caller can see.
DocumentRead.title: DocumentRead

DocumentSummaryRead.description:
One document without its body, as a listing answers it.

`can_edit` and `can_delete` say what this caller may do, so a client draws
the controls without repeating the rules.
DocumentSummaryRead.title: DocumentSummaryRead

DocumentTemplateListRead.description:
The document templates a project or initiative offers, and the ones its composers open with.

`default_document_template_id` is what a new document starts from and
`default_update_template_id` what the update composer opens with, each the
first of the project's teams to set one and always one of `templates`. An
initiative belongs to no team, so it carries neither.
DocumentTemplateListRead.title: DocumentTemplateListRead

DocumentVersionRead.description: An earlier title and body of a document, as it stood at the end of one edit session.
DocumentVersionRead.title: DocumentVersionRead

DownloadRead.description:
A presigned GET and when it stops working.

Minted per request and never stored or logged, so the window is the whole
guard on a URL that is a bearer credential until it expires.
DownloadRead.title: DownloadRead

DraftListRead.description: The caller's drafts, newest saved first.
DraftListRead.title: DraftListRead

DraftRead.description:
One of the caller's drafts, with the issue it sits on as a listing names it.

`parent_comment_id` is the root comment a reply draft answers, or null for a
draft on the issue itself. `issue_key` and `issue_title` are read at answer
time, so a moved or renamed issue never shows a stale one.

DraftWrite.description: The body a draft save takes, which replaces whatever the thread's draft held.
DraftWrite.title: DraftWrite

details.title: Details

error_code.title: Error Code

message.description: A human readable summary safe to surface to a caller.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

FavoriteFolderRead.description: One of the caller's favorite folders, `position` counting from 0 at the top.

FavoriteFolderWrite.description: A favorite folder's name, as creating or renaming one sends it.
FavoriteFolderWrite.title: FavoriteFolderWrite

FavoriteListRead.description: The caller's favorites in their order, each one they can still read, and their folders in theirs.
FavoriteListRead.title: FavoriteListRead

FavoriteOrder.description:
The caller's favorites in their new order.

Favorites the list leaves out keep their relative order after the named
ones, and names that are not favorites are ignored, so a reorder racing an
add or a removal in another tab never drops or resurrects anything.
`folders` orders the caller's folders by id the same way, and leaving it
out keeps the folders where they are.

One favorite as the sidebar draws it.

`title` is the issue title, or the name of the project, cycle, view, team,
document or initiative. `issue_key` and `status` are set for an issue, and
`team_key_prefix` wherever the target belongs to one team, which is what a
client builds a team or cycle link from. `icon` and `color` are the target's
own, where it has them. `folder_id` is the folder it sits in, or null at
the top level.

FavoriteRef.description:
One favorite named by its kind and id, as an add or a reorder sends it.

`team_id` is needed only for a cycle, whose key carries its team.
`folder_id` places the favorite in one of the caller's folders, and null
puts it at the top level. Left out, an add files a new favorite at the top
level and a reorder leaves the favorite in whatever folder it is in.
FavoriteRef.title: FavoriteRef

options, and it needs at least one.

HealthBreakdownRead.description: How many of an initiative's visible projects report each health.

One issue a project template adds, or one sub-issue an issue template adds under the new issue.

`key` names it inside the template, so `parent_key` can make it a sub-issue
of an issue listed before it and `milestone_key` can tie it to a milestone.
An issue template's sub-issues sit directly under the issue, so they carry
neither.
IssueBlueprint.title: IssueBlueprint

IssueBulkPatch.description:
The fields one bulk patch sets on every named issue.

The triage fields and the parent: a title, body or date is per issue by nature,
so a bulk write of one would be a mistake rather than a shortcut. Labels are an
add and a remove rather than a replacement, so tagging a selection keeps each
issue's other labels. `parent_id` nests every named issue under one parent, or
detaches them when null, under the single patch's same team and one level rules.

`archived` archives the selection when true and restores it when false, after
any field change in the same patch, so a selection is archived in one request
rather than one per issue.
IssueBulkPatch.title: IssueBulkPatch

IssueBulkRead.description:
What a bulk patch answers with.

`issues` is every written issue after the write, in request order. `skipped`
names any issue deleted between validation and its write, and any issue whose
estimate did not match `only_if_estimate`: validation is all or nothing, but
the writes are separate puts, and a concurrent delete or estimate change is
the one failure that can land between them.
IssueBulkRead.title: IssueBulkRead

IssueBulkUpdate.description:
The body `PATCH /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/issues` takes.

`only_if_estimate` writes only the issues whose estimate is that value right
now, `none` meaning unestimated, and reports the rest as skipped. It is checked
on the read and again as a condition on each write, so a peer setting an
estimate in between keeps their value rather than having it overwritten.
IssueBulkUpdate.title: IssueBulkUpdate

IssueConversionRead.description:
What converting an issue into a project answers with.

`project` is the new project, `issue` the original issue after it was closed
and pointed at the project, and `moved_issue_ids` the former sub-issues now in
the project, in creation order.

IssueCreate.description:
The body `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/issues` takes.

`team_id` is a field rather than a path segment because issues are workspace
scoped, which is what lets a link and a "my issues" read cross teams.
`template_id` fills every field the body leaves out from a template the team
offers, so `title` may be left out only when a template is named.
`form_answers` answers a form template's fields by key: text for a text or
select field and a boolean for a checkbox. `template_sub_issue_keys` keeps
only the template sub-issues it names; left out, every one is created.
IssueCreate.title: IssueCreate

ReleaseBackfill.description:
The body `POST .../teams/{team_id}/release-backfill` takes.

Rebuilds releases from one GitHub environment's past successful deployments,
newest first, a few per call. `repository` is a full name or id and defaults to
every repository pinned to the team. Pass `cursor` back until it comes back
null. A deployment that already has a release only gains missing issues, and
the backfill never moves issues or publishes GitHub Releases.

`deployment_ids` retries only those deployments, such as the
`unreadable_deployment_ids` an earlier page passed over, without paging
through history. It takes no cursor, and `repository` must name their
repository unless the team pins only one.
ReleaseBackfill.title: ReleaseBackfill

ReleaseBackfillRead.description:
What one backfill call did, and the cursor to continue from, null when it is done.

`deployments_skipped` counts deployments whose release had already reached
the stage, which cost no GitHub call. A page that stopped before its limit to
keep half the GitHub App's hourly budget for live sync, or to answer inside
the request timeout, sets `stopped_early` and says in `message` when to pass
the cursor back; `resume_after` is GitHub's budget reset when that is the
reason. `rate_limit_remaining` and `rate_limit` are GitHub's last word on the
installation's budget, and `github_calls` what this page spent of it.

`stalled` is set when the page recorded and skipped nothing, so passing the
cursor back moves only once the message's reason has passed.
`unreadable_deployment_ids` names deployments passed over because their range
could not be read inside the request timeout, and `pull_reads_skipped` counts
pull requests a recorded deployment did not read for keys for the same reason.
Pass `unreadable_deployment_ids` back as `deployment_ids` to retry only those.
A retry names in `deployments_not_found` the ids that are no successful
deployment of the environment in the repository.

`source` is `github_tag` or `github_release` for a page read from a
repository that records its releases from tags or GitHub Releases; its
deployment counts then count tags, and `unreadable_tags` names the tags
passed over because GitHub would not read them.
ReleaseBackfillRead.title: ReleaseBackfillRead

or ids, and from any team keys found in `commit_messages`, which is how a CI
job that knows only its git range links what it shipped. Recording a sha the

report a typo without the release being refused. `included_releases` are the
earlier releases a promotion carried, newest first, and `included_in_release`
is the promotion that carried this one.

get.description:
Bind a finished GitHub install to the workspace whose admin started it.

GitHub sends the browser here with `installation_id`, `setup_action` and the
`state` the install url carried, either as the Setup URL or, with user
authorization during installation on, as the Callback URL with a `code` added.
The workspace comes from the signed state alone and never from a query
parameter, the state is redeemed once, and the installation id is checked
against GitHub with the App JWT before anything is written. Whenever user
authorization is configured, a `code` is required and exchanged to ask GitHub
whether the person who came back can reach the installation: yes binds it even
when it predates the state, while no, no code or no answer refuses it. Only an
environment without user authorization falls back to the freshness check, which
reads the installation's `created_at` and never the caller's `setup_action`.
An `update` that GitHub sends with no state, because the change started on
GitHub, only refreshes an installation that is already bound, and an install
with no state, as when an organization owner approves a member's request, binds
nothing.

post.description:
Verify, claim and enqueue one GitHub delivery, then answer at once.

The order is the security property. The signature is checked over the raw body
before `json.loads` runs, so a forged delivery never reaches a parser. The
delivery id is then claimed in `idempotency`, which makes GitHub's redelivery
of a request whose response it never saw a no-op rather than a second set of
transitions. A failed enqueue releases the claim, so GitHub's redelivery of the
error it was answered does the work rather than being dropped as a replay.

the response cannot tell one from the other. The token alone is not enough:
the caller's verified address must be the one the invite was sent to, so a
forwarded or leaked link cannot join anyone else at the invited role.

The membership takes its plan slot, and the invite gives back its pending one,
in the same transaction as the two rows, so racing accepts at the last slot
land one member and refuse the rest.

The bearer is verified before the body is parsed, so an unauthenticated caller

the caller never authorized, or never in the named workspace, is a 404.

Delete the caller's account now.

A signed in person only, with their address typed out again, and refused with a
409 naming each workspace where they are the only owner and other people remain.
Once it passes, the account is marked deleted, so no sign in method or refresh
works for it any more, then every session, OAuth grant and personal API key is
revoked, the person's private agent profiles are removed, and the purge of
its data is started at once. The hourly sweep and the
queue's retries start any purge this request could not. The account's own
address is mailed, and the request is logged with how the caller last
authenticated. Repeating it for an account already deleted starts the purge again.

post.description:
Mint a key and show its plaintext, the only time it is ever shown.

A workspace key acts as the synthetic principal `svc#<workspace_id>` rather
than as its minter, but it still only works while that minter is an owner or
admin of the workspace, so a departure or demotion disables it. Only an admin
may mint one because it acts for the workspace rather than for a person.

The key row and the workspace's API key usage row are written in one
transaction, the usage row under a conditional increment, so two concurrent
mints at the limit cannot both land.

delete.description:
Revoke one key the caller owns, or any key for a workspace admin.

A key the caller neither owns nor administers is a 404 rather than a 403, so a
member cannot walk key ids to learn what other people hold.

A SCIM token is a 404 here too: it is listed and revoked on the single sign-on
settings, so a key listing never offers to revoke the directory's credential.

Revoking is idempotent: a key already revoked answers 204 rather than 404,
because the caller's intent is satisfied and a client retrying a revoke should
not have to distinguish the two.

post.description:
Record an uploaded object as an attachment, once it is really in the bucket.

The ticket is what proves the key was signed by this service for this caller on
this issue, so the recorded type and size are the ones S3 was told to enforce
rather than anything the commit body claims.

The object is checked for existence first, so a commit for an upload that never
happened is a 409 rather than a row pointing at nothing. Storage is checked again
here, because other uploads may have committed since the ticket was minted, and
the bytes are then reserved by one conditional write on the workspace's counter,
so two commits racing for the last bytes cannot both land.

post.description:
Mint a bounded presigned PUT, storing nothing on the issue yet.

The declared size is refused above the cap rather than quietly lowered, because
a client that declares 100 MB and receives a 25 MiB URL fails at the end of the
upload instead of the start. The same goes for the plan's pooled storage, which
the declared size is checked against before anything is signed.

The type is checked before signing rather than after the object lands: the type
goes into the signature, so refusing it here is what keeps the object from
existing at all.

Hang a link on an issue, deriving its favicon without fetching it.

The MVP does not crawl the target, so a title the caller does not give defaults
to the host and the favicon is a composed URL. Not fetching is the decision: a
crawl on a write path is a request the caller controls the destination of.

get.description:
One page of the issues the caller may see, filtered and sorted.

Every id filter repeats, ORing its values, and `none` matches the unset field
where the field can be unset. Filters are applied after the key read rather
than through an index, so adding one costs no GSI. The cursor is a position in
the filtered, sorted set and is bound to the filter, so a cursor carried to a
different filter starts over rather than skipping rows.

The exception is a filter on one person: `subscriber_id=me`, one `creator_id`
or one `assignee_id` reads that person's own index instead of every team, which
is what the My issues tabs ask for. Any other `subscriber_id` is matched after
the read, against the subscriptions of each person it names.

`match=any` keeps an issue meeting any one condition rather than all of them.
`groups` is a JSON array of condition objects, each holding these same filter
names plus its own `match`, and each counting as one condition, which is how
"status is Todo and (label is Bug or priority is Urgent)" is said. A group may
hold groups of its own, two levels at most, so a client can wrap its own
conditions in one group under the list's fixed scope. `content`
matches title and description text, `label_id_all` wants every label named,
and `completed_after` and `completed_before` bound the day an issue was done.
The `completed_desc` sort puts the latest `completed_at` first and issues not
completed last.
`customer_id` keeps the issues one of the named customers asked for and
`customer_id_not` drops them, `none` standing for no customer request and
`important` for an important one, and the `customer_requests_desc`,
`customer_important_desc` and `customer_revenue_desc` sorts put the most
requested, most importantly requested or highest revenue issues first.
Guests may use neither.

Archived issues are left out unless `include_archived` is set, and
`archived_only` lists nothing but them, the archive view. That read goes
straight to each status's archived partition of the status index rather than
reading every issue of the team and dropping the live ones. Issues awaiting
triage are left out the same way unless `include_triage` is set, and
`triage_only` lists nothing but them.

`include_sub_teams` with a `team_id` rolls that team's sub-teams the caller
may see into the list, so a parent team's views show its sub-teams' issues.
`reverse` turns the sort around, issues lacking the sorted value still last.
Each sub-issue carries its parent's `parent_key` and `parent_title`, so a row
listed apart from its parent can still name it.

Every body carries `synced_at`. Sent back as `updated_since` with the same
filter, it turns the read into a delta: only the issues changed since, every
one in the list's sort order and unpaged, plus `removed_ids` for issues that
left the filter, were archived or were deleted. `resync_required` asks for a
full read instead, when the cursor is older than deletions are remembered or
the delta is too large to carry. A delta costs one key-bounded query per team
on the change feed index, so a poll that finds nothing reads almost nothing.

A delta answer carries a weak `ETag` over its body. Two polls that find the
same thing answer the same body, so a poll that sends the tag back in
`If-None-Match` gets a 304 with no body instead. A full read carries none,
because its cursor moves with the clock.

fails the whole request with nothing changed. Each issue then goes through the
same write and activity path a single patch does, so history cannot tell a bulk
edit from one issue edited at a time. `archived` then archives or restores each
issue through the single-issue archive path, with the same team membership rule.

get.description:
Saved views the caller may read, narrowed by scope and, with `entity`, to issue or project views.

`all` is the caller's own views plus the team views of teams they can see,
which for a guest is only the teams they hold a membership in, so the listing
is built from what they may read rather than filtered afterwards. The
answer carries a weak `ETag`, so an unchanged poll gets a 304.

post.description:
Save a new view, personal unless it names a team.

A team view needs the caller to be a member of that team: a reader could
otherwise leave a shared view on a team they cannot write in.

get.description:
The caller's workspace home: their focus, their teams' cycles, projects, what shipped and the inbox.

`tz` is the caller's IANA timezone, which decides what today is for due
dates and cycles. Every list is bounded, so the read costs the same on a
quiet workspace and a busy one.

Issue count or estimate points grouped by one dimension, optionally segmented by a second.

Takes the issue list's filters with the same meaning. With `view_id` the saved
view's team and live filter apply as well, ANDed with any filter sent. With
neither a team nor a view, every team the caller can see is counted. A scope
holding more than `row_cap` issues answers over the issues read with
`truncated` set rather than reading without bound.

One member's page header: name, avatar, role and the teams of theirs the caller can see.

A 404 when they are not a member of this workspace. No email is returned.

One page of a member's issue changes and comments, newest first.

Only rows on issues the caller can read are returned, so a page can be short
while `next_cursor` still walks the whole history.
